function: Channel estimation (denoising) with a DVAE-ATT plus learnable link management, the power split between direct and indirect links, trained on sum rate and reconstruction loss (p. 9).
system: Reflecting IRS-assisted mmWave massive MIMO-OFDM downlink: BS with M=32 or 64 antennas, 1-10 single-antenna UEs, N IRS elements (number and carrier not stated) (pp. 5, 10, 12).
method: Denoising variational autoencoder with attention (DVAE-ATT) plus trainable link-management weights; supervised end-to-end training with negative sum rate, KL and MSE reconstruction loss (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Simulated with MATLAB nrCDLChannel (3GPP TR 38.901 CDL); 60,500 samples split 45,000 train, 5,000 validation, 10,500 test (p. 9).
test_conditions: Held-out split of same simulated data, model trained separately per SNR (p. 10); sum rate swept over 1-10 users and radii 5-35 m (p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned: SCA [18], static direct/indirect ratio without LM. Learned: CV-DnCNN [19], SPR-CNN [20], DAE [36], DAE-CNN-ATT [21], SPARSE-MATT-DAE [22] (p. 10).
metrics: Sum rate and NMSE versus SNR, number of users and radius; error heatmaps; channel magnitude versus subcarrier index (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Table 2 gives big-O complexity for all schemes; DVAE-ATT O((M·h1 + Σ hl·hl+1 + hL·K) + di·M²·K), stated lowest; SCA O(n^3.5) (pp. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 9: "nrCDLChannel package, a system object tailored for simulating clustered delay line (CDL) MIMO fading channels, as specified by the 3GPP Technical Report TR 38.901"; the 60,500-sample dataset is used for training and testing.
q2_support: p. 10: "the model is trained separately for each specific SNR value"; p. 12 sweeps users and radius at fixed 64 antennas and 5 dB with no stated train/test mismatch; the test set is a held-out 10,500-sample split of the same data (p. 9).
q3_support: p. 10: "40% enhancement over SCA" (non-learned optimization) and "7% enhancement over SPARSE-MATT-DAE" (earlier learned, same authors), also CV-DnCNN, SPR-CNN and DAE, compared on sum rate and NMSE (Figs. 3-4).
q4_support: p. 12: "our proposed DVAE-ATT model achieves the lowest computational complexity in this comparison"; Table 2 and the text give the order O((M·h1 + Σ hl·hl+1 + hL·K) + di·M²·K).
q5_support: p. 9: "We generated our dataset using" MATLAB nrCDLChannel; no link to code or data and no public channel dataset appear anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included. Area 2 vs 3 for the reviewer: the paper states that "maximizing the sum rate is the primary objective" (p. 9) and link management sets the direct/indirect power split (area 3 function), but the learned network is a channel estimator compared with channel estimators on NMSE and sum rate (pp. 9-10); area 2 chosen. q1 comes from the simulation section (CDL, TR 38.901, p. 9) although the system model uses Saleh-Valenzuela (p. 5). IRS element count and carrier frequency are not stated.
